**Silvio Berlusconi and Mediaset**
A billionaire media tycoon who founded Mediaset, Italy's largest private broadcaster, and owned major newspapers. He served as Prime Minister several times between 1994 and 2011, including 2001–2006 and from 2008, and dominated Italian politics for two decades.

**"Bunga bunga"**
The term Berlusconi allegedly used for the sex parties held at his villa. The scandal, which included charges involving an underage dancer, contributed to his downfall as Prime Minister in 2011.

**Matteo Salvini**
Leader of the right-wing League and Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister from 2018 to 2019. He is known for hardline anti-immigration policies, such as closing Italian ports to migrant rescue ships, and for feuding with French President Emmanuel Macron, saying that "Macron shouldn't lecture others."

**Lega (Northern League)**
A right-wing populist party founded as the Lega Nord, which originally sought autonomy or even independence for northern Italy. Under Salvini it dropped "Nord" and became a national anti-immigration party. It was part of Berlusconi's governing coalition in 2008.

**Giorgia Meloni**
Leader of the far-right Brothers of Italy party, who became Italy's first female Prime Minister in October 2022 after Mario Draghi's government collapsed.

**Mario Draghi ("Super Mario")**
An economist who was President of the European Central Bank from 2011 to 2019 and was nicknamed "Super Mario" for saving the euro by pledging to do "whatever it takes." He led a national unity government as Prime Minister from 2021 until he resigned in 2022.

**Matteo Renzi ("The Scrapper")**
A center-left Prime Minister from 2014 to 2016, nicknamed "Il Rottamatore" (The Scrapper) for his promise to scrap Italy's old political class. He resigned after voters rejected his constitutional reform in a December 2016 referendum.

**People of Freedom (Il Popolo della Libertà)**
The center-right party led by Berlusconi, formed by merging his Forza Italia with other right-wing parties. In April 2008 it won the election alongside the Northern League, making Berlusconi Prime Minister of Italy's sixty-second government since World War II.

**Pamela Mastropietro**
An 18-year-old woman killed and dismembered in Macerata in 2018. A Nigerian migrant was convicted of her murder, and Salvini has often cited the case to defend his anti-immigration stance.

**Lorenzo Fontana**
A League politician who became President (Speaker) of the Chamber of Deputies in 2022. He is a strongly conservative Catholic who called himself "an identitarian fighting rootless financial elites" and dismissed alternatives to traditional marriage as "disgusting."

**Cécile Kyenge**
A Congolese-born doctor who became Italy's first black government minister, serving as Minister for Integration in 2013. She was the target of racist insults from League politicians and became involved in defamation disputes with them.

**"Roma ladrona" ("Thieving Rome")**
A slogan of the Northern League, which accused the national government in Rome of stealing tax money from the hardworking north. League figures such as Umberto Bossi also made extreme anti-immigrant statements, including calls to use force against migrant boats.

**The Caste (La Casta)**
A 2007 bestselling book by journalists Gian Antonio Stella and Sergio Rizzo exposing the privileges and waste of Italy's political class. It fed widespread public anger at politicians and boosted anti-establishment movements.
